groups.text: It is currently a clear morning in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 24 degrees.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Google is dismantling the independence of DeepMind, turning the AI lab into a subsidiary and moving all Gemini development to the Bay Area. Founder Demis Hassabis may leave the company in the coming months, while researcher Koray Kavukcuoglu takes over day-to-day operations without the CEO title. Some experts view this restructuring as a strategic pivot toward cloud infrastructure, though others suggest Google is falling behind in the race for leading AI models. Separately, a video has resurfaced on X claiming to show Nigerian Army personnel destroying farmland after residents confronted Fulani herders. The footage gained thousands of views and sparked comments about institutional distrust and ethnic tensions. However, fact-checkers have verified that the clip dates back to 2021. At that time, the Nigerian Army debunked the video as a doctored clip designed to denigrate its personnel.

The General Staff of Ukraine's Armed Forces reports that Russia has lost approximately 1,457,740 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,130 casualties suffered by Russian forces over the past day alone. The report also lists massive equipment losses, including over 12,000 tanks and more than 451,000 unmanned aerial vehicles. While Ukraine maintains operational secrecy regarding its own losses, a January 2026 report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated Ukrainian casualties between 500,000 and 600,000 through December 2025. Separately, in Nigeria, the fact-checking organization Dubawa has spent the last week debunking viral misinformation. They verified that a video claiming to show a new terrorist group in Nigeria actually depicted political movements in South Sudan. Dubawa also found no evidence for claims that the Sultan of Sokoto endorsed President Bola Tinubu for a second term.

In British Columbia, the provincial government has declared a state of emergency as wildfires tear through the Rocky Mountains. Authorities have issued 38 evacuation orders and 49 warnings for more than 100 fires, forcing over 20,000 people to leave their homes. The situation is particularly dire in the Okanagan Valley wine and fruit-growing region, where the Bald-Range fire expanded to roughly 9,500 hectares in a short window due to strong winds. Premier David Eby warns that conditions are extremely dangerous, noting that some residents have been trapped by flames and require rescue by helicopter. Meanwhile, in Japan, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is traveling to Nagasaki this Sunday to meet with atomic bomb survivors. This visit comes as several Japanese leaders call for a renewed debate on nuclear deterrence, specifically seeking to review the long-standing principle that prohibits the introduction of nuclear weapons onto Japanese territory.

A professionally built drone equipped with explosives recently targeted the Leipzig/Halle airport. A criminal officer wearing a visor and protective clothing had to defuse the device alongside an explosive-disposal robot. The drone was technically designed to be difficult to detect, and investigators believe a second drone may have acted as a signal amplifier. This suggests the involvement of professional actors rather than amateurs. While DHL operated its own detection systems at the site, the Federal Police only visibly increased their capacities after the incident occurred. This gap in security highlights a tension between rapid technological advances in drone warfare and Germany's current defensive architecture. Experts warn that small aircraft can now deliver significant explosive power over long distances with minimal effort. The situation remains critical as authorities investigate who was behind the attack and why official detection systems failed to spot the device first.

Misleading claims are circulating on Facebook alleging that Nigeria has banned preaching in commercial buses. This is not an existing ban, but rather a proposed legislative amendment to the Federal Road Safety Commission Act that suggests a 50,000 naira fine for those convicted of preaching, trading, or hawking in buses. In other news, X users are discovering they can be found by others via their phone numbers or email addresses through specific discoverability privacy settings. While many assume you must ask for a username to become mutuals, these settings allow contacts to find accounts automatically unless the user explicitly turns them off. Shifting to sports in Brazil, Red Bull Bragantino and Corinthians face off today for the twenty-second round of the Brasileirão. The match kicks off at 6:30 Brasília time at the Estádio Municipal Cícero de Souza Marques in Bragança, with live coverage provided by Premiere.

Researchers have achieved a first in synthetic biology by using genome language models to design viable bacteriophage genomes. While these models had previously been used for smaller biological systems, their ability to generate functional sequences at the scale of whole genomes remained untested until now. To reach this milestone, the team leveraged frontier models known as Evo 1 and Evo 2, using the lytic phage ΦX174 as a design template. The goal was to create whole-genome sequences that maintained realistic genetic architectures while achieving specific host tropism. When these AI-generated genomes moved from digital design to experimental testing, the results yielded sixteen viable phages. These new biological entities demonstrate substantial evolutionary novelty, marking a shift in how scientists can program functional genetic material from the ground up using generative artificial intelligence.

A new study suggests that obesity may be responsible for far more cancer cases than previously understood. Researchers led by Hermann Brenner at the German Cancer Research Center found that up to 11.5 percent of cancers could be attributable to being overweight. This figure is a significant increase over previous estimates, which placed the risk between 2 and 8 percent. The team discovered that abdominal fat specifically increases these risks, particularly among women. Being overweight or obese significantly raises the likelihood of developing liver, breast, and colon cancer, while acting as a major risk factor for ten other types of cancer. To reach these conclusions, the researchers moved away from using body mass index, which fails to distinguish between muscle and fat or show how fat is distributed throughout the body. Michael Leitzmann of the University of Regensburg notes that this updated research questions whether the link has been underestimated until now.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain clear with temperatures between 25 and 31 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has an all-day event for the twenty-twenty-six summer holidays in Berlin.
Mail worth checking: AlgorithmWatch needs you to confirm your email for the Schufa request. Also, you have a response from Kleinanzeigen regarding the cargo trailer.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
